extraction.source: app/data/Sources/Design codes/Design code rules - East Riding.csv
extraction.method: Converted from the spreadsheet export by scripts/csv-to-json.js. Sections come from the web page each rule links to (…entry=3_3_… is section 3.3), named after their national design issue; chapters are named after the issue's group. The spreadsheet gives some rules the same reference, so those have -1, -2… added; printed-reference keeps the spreadsheet's. Place types and development types are kept from the hand-extracted file (scripts/design-codes/east-riding.json) and matched to the spreadsheet's text.

design-code.name: East Riding Design Code
design-code.description: The East Riding Design Code has been prepared to clarify design expectations and improve the quality of new development across the whole of the East Riding of Yorkshire.
design-code.vision: Green, inclusive and distinctive places, which connect landscape, people, place and nature. New development in the East Riding will celebrate the diversity of the built and natural environment and its heritage to create healthy and sustainable places for the communities of today and tomorrow.
design-code.coverage: The whole of the East Riding of Yorkshire
design-code.credits: Illustrations by Harper Perry Ltd; Illustrations by Joseph Cox, FORM Studio
design-code.local-development-document: Supplementary Planning Document (SPD) – East Riding Design Code, adopted Apr 2025 (minor updates Sep 2025); material consideration

design-code-sections.name: New industrial, storage and distribution (ISDC) buildings

design-code-rules.title: Multifunctional green infrastructure network
design-code-rules.requirement-text: A connected, multifunctional green infrastructure (GI) network should be integrated into the landscape design, combining public open space, movement, SuDS and wildlife networks and blending with GI beyond the site.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: GI should serve several functions at once (recreation, movement, drainage, biodiversity). It should link existing and proposed natural spaces (woodland, hedgerows, habitats, green corridors, SuDS, water bodies) and integrate with neighbouring/future development. Urban Greening Factor targets: 0.3 commercial, 0.4 residential, 0.5 residential greenfield; UGF calculation evidence must be submitted.

supporting-documents.listed-as: Green Infrastructure Planning and Design Guide
Urban Greening Factor for England User Guide

design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Rule wording appears only in a figure image (Figure 19) on the web page – text here is summarised from the surrounding guidance. Applies-to list from figure caption.

design-code-rules.title: Connected wildlife habitats
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Throughout the whole site, including public and private spaces, development should: [create a connected network of existing and new wildlife habitats linked into the green and blue infrastructure].
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Retain and enhance natural features; use native, climate-resistant planting; integrate SuDS; consider green walls, green and brown roofs; include bat and swift bricks and species-specific nest boxes (avoid generic bird boxes). Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG) metrics must be submitted with applications.
design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Web page cites ENV4 (sites of importance for biodiversity) as well as ENV1/S9; Appendix D lists ENV5.

design-code-rules.title: Retaining category A and B trees
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Existing category A and B trees within the development site must be retained.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Category C trees should be retained where possible to support biodiversity. Any removals must be justified in the supporting documents.

supporting-documents.listed-as: TDAG – First Steps in Trees and Development

design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Tree categories per BS5837 arboricultural survey.

design-code-rules.title: Replacing removed trees 2 for 1
design-code-rules.requirement-text: When there is the need to remove existing trees (of any category) they must be replaced on-site on a 1:2 ratio.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Replacement trees should be planted no later than the next available planting season after the relevant phase is completed. Extra heavy or heavy standard trees suggested for streets; pre-application advice available.

supporting-documents.listed-as: TDAG – First Steps in Trees and Development

design-code-rules.title: New trees in the public realm
design-code-rules.requirement-text: A minimum of 75% of new trees planted as part of landscaping proposals must be within the public realm.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Public realm planting (including public streets) is intended to secure retention and management of trees over their lifespan.

supporting-documents.listed-as: TDAG – First Steps in Trees and Development

design-code-rules.title: Tree-lined new streets
design-code-rules.requirement-text: New streets must be tree-lined.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Street trees should be planted so they can grow without damaging surrounding highway infrastructure (see TDAG guidance on street trees).

supporting-documents.listed-as: TDAG – First Steps in Trees and Development

design-code-rules.title: Retaining and adding trees and hedgerows
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Trees and hedgerows should be retained and their provision should be increased wherever possible.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Tree planting should reflect native and climate-resistant species (see TDAG guidance). Statement continues with reference to holistic benefits and wellbeing.

supporting-documents.listed-as: TDAG – First Steps in Trees and Development

design-code-rules.title: Sustainable drainage in the site layout
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Sustainable drainage systems (SuDS) must be embedded in the site layout and be fully integrated within the green infrastructure system.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: SuDS should be built into plots, streets, public open spaces and wildlife networks; use natural site slopes to reduce mechanical measures, manage runoff, improve filtration/infiltration and provide storage for irrigation; maximise biodiversity. On sites with nutrient-neutrality issues SuDS may not be suitable – take a site-specific approach. Table 3 sets suitability of SuDS methods by development type and location (plot/street/POS); Table 4 is a glossary of methods.

supporting-documents.listed-as: ERYC SuDS and Surface Water Drainage for New Developments

design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Image alt text: 'Relevant to all development'. Opening words of rule reconstructed from context – check figure.

design-code-rules.title: On-site renewable energy for new buildings
design-code-rules.requirement-text: At least one form of on-site renewable energy must be delivered where development includes new buildings.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Supports the Council's Climate Change Strategy 2022-2030. Solutions can be plot-based or larger-scale, must fit their context, avoid overbearing visual impact and noise. Buildings should also be designed to be as energy efficient as possible.

supporting-documents.listed-as: Historic England – Adapting Historic Buildings for Energy and Carbon Efficiency

design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Alt text lists '1-2 units, 10+ units, Mixed Use, 25+ units…' (3-9 units not listed – likely a source error). Image file named g5.png.

design-code-rules.title: Energy efficiency of existing buildings
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Work to existing buildings should improve energy efficiency, e.g. by retrofitting insulation and low-carbon technology.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Domestic properties account for c.18% of East Riding greenhouse gas emissions; retrofitting insulation and technology to improve energy efficiency is recommended.

supporting-documents.listed-as: Historic England – Adapting Historic Buildings for Energy and Carbon Efficiency

design-code-rules.extraction-notes: G4 is labelled only in image alt text – no separate rule text on the web page; summarised from guidance. Heritage buildings: see Historic England guidance.

design-code-rules.title: Protecting views to landmarks
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Views to and between identified landmarks (built and natural) must be preserved and enhanced by direct and indirect lines of sight.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Consider common views such as street terminations and ensure attractive/prominent features occupy them. Consider effects on views from landmarks beyond the site's red line.

supporting-documents.listed-as: Conservation Area Appraisals and Management Plans
Historic England – Understanding Place: Historic Area Assessments

design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Shown as 'C07' on page; remainder of rule abridged.

design-code-rules.title: Responding to surrounding scale and grain
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Scale, proportions and urban grain should respond to surrounding development and the place-type visions in Chapter 2.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Gently increasing density may suit locations close to services and transport hubs. Block and plot sizes per place type are in Chapters 6 and 8. Out-of-character existing development should not be used as a precedent (clarify at pre-application stage). Transitions between place types should be gradual – streets and public open space can act as transition points.
design-code-rules.area-text: All place types (transitions between place types)

supporting-documents.listed-as: Conservation Area Appraisals and Management Plans
Historic England – Understanding Place: Historic Area Assessments

design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Labelled in alt text only; no separate rule statement.

design-code-rules.title: Articulated corner plots
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Corner plots must include a form of articulation.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Corners can be marked with a prominent building or change in building/plot line; articulation via height, recessed/projecting facades, material detailing, window/door surrounds, landscaping or setbacks creating public space. Higher-priority corners need more articulation. As a minimum every elevation facing a street or public space needs windows and doors overlooking it.
design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Shown as 'C08'.

design-code-rules.title: Easy-to-navigate layouts
design-code-rules.requirement-text: All elements of a development should help make the layout legible and easy to navigate.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Key services, social infrastructure, landmark buildings and public open spaces should sit on primary or secondary routes. Higher street hierarchy = larger buildings and less setback variation. On larger sites plan bus routes/stops with direct active-travel routes, resting space and overlooking. Prioritise walkers, wheelers, riders and cyclists.
design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Shown as 'G06'; no separate rule statement.

design-code-rules.title: Connecting to the street hierarchy
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Proposed streets must connect only to a street type of the same rank, or one step up or down the street hierarchy (Tables 5 and 6).
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Connecting more than one step up/down (e.g. tertiary to primary) is not appropriate; transitions should be gradual to support legibility, permeability and active travel. Connected streets need not be through-routes for motor vehicles, but should keep walking, cycling and wheeling connections.
design-code-rules.area-text: All place types (per Table 5 street types)

design-code-rules.title: Appropriate street types
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Development must incorporate only the appropriate street types as per Table 5.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Table 6 describes each street type and sets dwelling limits: Local Distributors 400+ dwellings; Local Streets 51-200; Mews, Residential Access, Rural Edge and Rural Residential Lane max 50. Table 10 (7.6) gives construction details per street type.
design-code-rules.area-text: Varies by place type – Table 5 sets permitted street types for Town Centre, Inner Neighbourhood, Outer Neighbourhood, Neighbourhood Centre, Village, Industrial/Storage & Distribution, Minor Commercial, Major Commercial
design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Alt text lists 3-9, 10-24, 25+ units, Flats, ISD, Commercial (mapped to standard types here).

design-code-rules.title: Joining existing street, path and cycle networks
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Development must integrate with the existing street, footpath and cycle network. Space to facilitate future connections, using an appropriate street in the hierarchy, must be included.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Avoid overly long routes, especially for active travel. New streets max 10% gradient. Edge-of-site buildings need enough separation for future through-connections, using primary, secondary or local street types. Interim uses for link spaces: landscaping, temporary POS or visitor parking.

supporting-documents.listed-as: Public Rights of Way and Planning Guidance
Local Cycling and Walking Infrastructure Plans
Paths for All – Outdoor Accessibility Guidance

design-code-rules.title: Footways and cycle paths on new streets
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Accessible footways and cycle paths (connecting to existing adjoining networks) must be delivered on all new streets.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Safe, direct routes for walking, wheeling, riding and cycling following desire lines. Cycle path requirements vary by street hierarchy (Table 12, section 7.6). Retain public rights of way, ideally in a green corridor.

supporting-documents.listed-as: Public Rights of Way and Planning Guidance
Local Cycling and Walking Infrastructure Plans
Paths for All – Outdoor Accessibility Guidance

design-code-rules.title: Integrated affordable units
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Affordable units (residential and non-residential) must be fully integrated and not differentiated by siting or design.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Consider siting early in layout. Specialist units may need specific locations (e.g. older people's housing near services/transport; affordable workshops away from homes).

design-code-rules.title: Flexible ground floors
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Ground floors should allow for flexibility: increased floor-to-ceiling heights in centres, and units that can convert to non-residential use elsewhere.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: (1) Town and Neighbourhood Centres: increase ground-floor floor-to-ceiling heights to allow future uses and extra heating/cooling/ventilation plant; taller buildings help define hierarchy. (2) Elsewhere: consider units on primary streets and corner plots that can easily convert to non-residential use.
design-code-rules.area-text: Part 1: Town Centre, Neighbourhood Centre. Part 2: all other place types
design-code-rules.extraction-notes: No separate rule statement on page.

design-code-rules.title: Public spaces that reflect local character
design-code-rules.requirement-text: The design of public spaces should reflect local character and draw from well-designed local references.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Reflect character through formality, enclosure, arrangement of features, plant species and boundary treatments. Incorporate trees, hedgerows and SuDS; may include ponds/water features.
design-code-rules.area-text: Formal (Town Centre); Semi-formal (Neighbourhood Centre); Informal (Outer Neighbourhood) – Figure 35
design-code-rules.national-design-issue: Public open space - Public open space character
design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Flats listed in alt text.

design-code-rules.title: Benches in parks and gardens
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Benches must be provided in public parks and gardens at a minimum of every 100 metres along main footpaths (300 metres on other routes).
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Benches preferred; informal perches where space is limited. Seating should be appealing, warm to sit on, in high-footfall, overlooked spots, not blocking paths, with space alongside for wheelchair users. Larger spaces: mix of picnic, sheltered and facing seats.
design-code-rules.area-text: Public parks and gardens (all place types)
design-code-rules.national-design-issue: Public open space - Design for all

design-code-rules.title: Footpath gradients
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Gradients to footpaths must be less than 1:20.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Provide a resting point and landing for every 0.75 m of level change; landings at least as long as the path is wide with accessible seating. Also follow section 7.2.
design-code-rules.national-design-issue: Public open space - Design for all

design-code-rules.title: Inclusive public spaces
design-code-rules.requirement-text: The following design requirements should be followed for all new public space: [easy to reach for all, overlooked, welcoming, signed and lit, varied spaces with sun and shade, seating, SuDS, retained mature landscape and planting].
design-code-rules.guidance-text: New public open space should be accessible to everyone including from outside the site. Table 7 lists further features by place type (tick marks not readable from web page).
design-code-rules.area-text: All place types (Table 7 adds features by place type)
design-code-rules.national-design-issue: Public open space - Design for all

design-code-rules.title: Formal and informal play
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Public open space should offer both formal and informal play, with dedicated play areas designed to a holistic, inclusive concept.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Play locations matched to user groups; diverse play types; consider ages, abilities and genders; accessible/inclusive equipment; all-weather use; hard-wearing, low-maintenance materials. Use Scope's Play Investigation to test universal design.
design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Presented as 'Key guidance' – no separate rule statement.

design-code-rules.title: Facilities for outdoor sport
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Outdoor sports facilities and playing pitches should have nearby changing facilities and accessible parking, with floodlighting impacts mitigated.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Changing facilities close to pitches with visual impact mitigated; accessible car and cycle parking no more than 300 m from pitches and changing; mitigate floodlighting on residential areas; follow Sport England guidance.
design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Presented as 'Key guidance'.

design-code-rules.title: Overlooked public open space
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Public Open Spaces must be overlooked directly by neighbouring buildings; frontages must address the public open space and boundary treatments must not stop visibility.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Passive surveillance via windows and doors from a range of uses, low-level boundaries, no dead ends or blind corners, communal parking and lighting (Figure 37).
design-code-rules.national-design-issue: Public open space - Safety and surveillance

design-code-rules.title: Block forms for the place type
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Block forms must be appropriate for the place type in which the development site is located, as set out in Table 8.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Block forms should reinforce the positive characteristics of each place type, so only certain forms (Perimeter, Terraced, Courtyard, Irregular) are supported in each.
design-code-rules.area-text: Varies by place type – Table 8 (Town Centre, Inner Neighbourhood, Outer Neighbourhood, Neighbourhood Centre, Village, Countryside)
design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Table 8 tick marks not readable from web page text – check source.

design-code-rules.title: Maximum block length
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Block lengths must not exceed 160 metres.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Block sizes should improve active-travel connectivity and follow adjacent blocks. Transition areas may be more flexible but still under 160 m. Widths should follow plot depths giving good private amenity; avoid excessive central courtyards; rear habitable windows should overlook the whole courtyard (Figure 40).
design-code-rules.area-text: All place types (more flexibility in transition areas)

design-code-rules.title: Location of breaks in blocks
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Breaks in the block for public active travel access must be located centrally, and no more than 80 metres from a parallel street.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Snickets, alleyways and ginnels shape local urban grain. Breaks must be well designed, legible as public routes and feel safe.

design-code-rules.title: Overlooked breaks in blocks
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Any breaks in a block, including for private access only, must benefit from passive surveillance.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Windows/doors overlooking shared and public space, low boundaries, no dead ends/blind corners, communal parking in the block, lighting. Limit private accesses; shared access points preferred; gates can distinguish public/private.

design-code-rules.title: Active frontages
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Buildings must have active frontages.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Active ground-floor uses (shops, cafés, community uses, studios/workshops); residential/office above adds surveillance. Main entrances and windows face the street; upper-floor windows/balconies overlook it where appropriate.
design-code-rules.area-text: All place types – highest level in Town and Neighbourhood Centres (active ground floor uses, high glazing, balconies – not usually in conservation areas); residential areas: doors and windows face street

design-code-rules.title: Minimum footway width
design-code-rules.requirement-text: New footways must be a minimum width of 2 metres. Narrower sections must be at least 1 m wide and not continue for more than 6 m.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Minimum widths only – see C31/Table 12 for shared paths. Utility access away from high footfall; dropped kerbs at junctions/desire lines; tactile paving; street furniture leaving 2 m clear; gradient ideally ≤5%; ramps wherever steps; 2.6 m vertical clearance. Planted verges improve safety, biodiversity, drainage and deter footway parking.

supporting-documents.listed-as: DfT – Crossing Selector Tool User Manual
RNIB – Key Principles of Inclusive Street Design
Living Streets – Inclusive Design at Continuous Footways
Highways Design Guide pp.26 & 28 (no link on page)

design-code-rules.title: Level footways behind dropped kerbs
design-code-rules.requirement-text: A continuous levelled footway at least 1.2 m wide must be provided behind a dropped kerb.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Changes in path level make movement difficult for people with impaired vision, wheelchair users and those pushing prams.

supporting-documents.listed-as: DfT – Crossing Selector Tool User Manual
RNIB – Key Principles of Inclusive Street Design
Living Streets – Inclusive Design at Continuous Footways
Highways Design Guide pp.26 & 28 (no link on page)

design-code-rules.title: Continuous crossings at side streets
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Continuous crossings must be used at the mouths of junctions with lower-order streets in Town Centres and Neighbourhood Centres.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Should also be used in Inner/Outer Neighbourhoods and Villages, especially on busy routes (schools, shops, parks). Surface to match and be as wide as the footway; prioritise pedestrians, slow traffic (ramps, narrowing); tactile paving.
design-code-rules.area-text: Mandatory: Town Centre, Neighbourhood Centre. Recommended: Inner Neighbourhood, Outer Neighbourhood, Village

supporting-documents.listed-as: DfT – Crossing Selector Tool User Manual
RNIB – Key Principles of Inclusive Street Design
Living Streets – Inclusive Design at Continuous Footways
Highways Design Guide pp.26 & 28 (no link on page)

design-code-rules.title: Benches in town centres
design-code-rules.requirement-text: A minimum of one bench every 100 metres must be provided in town centres.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Benches preferred as resting points; informal perches where space is limited. Benches should be appealing, warm to sit on, in the landscaping plan, on high-footfall, well-surveilled routes, not obstructing footways (see C22), with space for wheelchair users.
design-code-rules.national-design-issue: Streets - Resting points and street furniture

supporting-documents.listed-as: Paths for All – Outdoor Accessibility Guidance (Part B)

design-code-rules.title: Positioning street furniture
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Any street furniture must be located a minimum of 0.45 metres from the edge of the highway, maintaining a minimum 1 metre unobstructed footway.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Keeps streets safe and accessible for all users (see C22).
design-code-rules.national-design-issue: Streets - Resting points and street furniture

supporting-documents.listed-as: Paths for All – Outdoor Accessibility Guidance (Part B)

design-code-rules.title: Street enclosure
design-code-rules.requirement-text: The level of enclosure should be the highest possible once all other functions, footways, cycleways and parking [and other Design Code requirements] are accommodated.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Enclosure created by buildings and street trees – boundary treatments not suitable. In conservation areas match surrounding context. Higher enclosure typical in town/village centres, lower toward settlement edges (Figure 48).
design-code-rules.area-text: All place types (higher in town and village centres, lower at settlement edges)

design-code-rules.title: Matching a uniform building line
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Where there is a universal building line on a street, any infill development must match the existing building line.

design-code-rules.title: Variation from a mixed building line
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Where there is a varied building line any variation from the predominant building line must be as set out in Table 9.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Variation encouraged at regular/irregular intervals unless C27 applies. Principal elevations should front the building line (see 7.1). Table 9 permitted variation: Town Centre ±0.5 m; Inner Neighbourhood ±0.5 m; Outer Neighbourhood ±3 m; Neighbourhood Centre ±1 m (terraced blocks ±0.5 m); Village ±3 m.
design-code-rules.area-text: Varies by place type – Town Centre, Inner Neighbourhood, Outer Neighbourhood, Neighbourhood Centre, Village (Table 9)

design-code-rules.title: Setting a new building line
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Where there is no existing building line, a new building line must be set back from the front of the plot as set out in Table 9.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Building lines vary less higher up the street hierarchy. Setbacks support legibility (4.2). Table 9 maximum new setback: Town Centre 0.5 m; Inner Neighbourhood 1.5 m; Outer Neighbourhood 5 m; Neighbourhood Centre 1 m; Village 3 m.
design-code-rules.area-text: Varies by place type – Town Centre, Inner Neighbourhood, Outer Neighbourhood, Neighbourhood Centre, Village (Table 9)

design-code-rules.title: Carriageway widths and radii
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Carriageway widths and radii must be as set out in Table 10.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Use minimum effective width/radii. Table 10 covers widths, radii, access points, junction spacing and construction by street type (e.g. Local Distributor 5.5-6.3 m; High Street max 5 m; Industrial Connector max 7.3 m; Mews 5 m shared surface + 2 m service strip; bus routes min 6.75 m). Check visibility against Table 11 (e.g. 20 mph 2.4 x 25 m; 30 mph 2.4 x 43 m). Avoid cul-de-sacs; where unavoidable max 35 dwellings with turning area. Discuss bus routes with public transport officer pre-submission.
design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Exceptions must be justified in the compliance checklist.

design-code-rules.title: Cycleway design
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Cycleways must be as set out in Table 12.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Integrate with wider network; no abrupt ends. LTN 1/20 segregation from motor traffic and pedestrians. Table 12: Primary/High Street segregated to LTN 1/20; Local Connector shared 3 m path one side + 2 m other; Local Street 2 m footpaths both sides (3 m one side >100 dwellings); Mews shared surface + 2 m service strip. Avoid spiky/fast-growing planting next to lanes.

design-code-rules.title: Speed reduction on streets
design-code-rules.requirement-text: On high streets, local streets and tertiary streets, at least one speed-reduction method must be built into the street design.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Also use traffic calming near schools, playing fields, parks, community facilities and bus stops. Spacing (Table 13): Primary 80 m; Local (51-100 dwellings) 60 m; Tertiary 40 m. Methods: alignment changes, staggered junctions (offset ≤1 m from tangent), regular junction/crossing spacing, narrower carriageways, tree/SuDS build-outs, landscaped on-street parking, shared surfaces. Speed bumps last resort.
design-code-rules.area-text: All place types (high streets, local and tertiary streets)

design-code-rules.title: Parking provision
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Parking must be provided as set out in Table 15.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Parking should suit location, type and scale – avoid over- and under-provision. Public car parks should meet the Park Mark scheme. Not applicable to householder development, but loss of a space through an extension may matter.
design-code-rules.area-text: Varies by place type – Table 15: higher rates in Town Centre, Inner Neighbourhood, Neighbourhood Centre than Outer Neighbourhood, Village, Countryside (e.g. 3-4 bed: 2 vs 3 spaces)

design-code-rules.title: Landscaping parking
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Landscaping must be incorporated to reduce the visual impact of parking.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Landscaping in public areas and private plots; low maintenance, not affecting visibility; can combine with SuDS (3.4).

design-code-rules.title: Non-residential and street parking bay sizes
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Non-residential and street parking bays must meet the minimum sizes as set out in Table 14.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: On-street parallel bays in a layby or widened carriageway, clearly marked. Traffic Regulation Orders may be needed near schools, hospitals etc. (usually legal agreement and cost).

design-code-rules.title: Motorcycle parking
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Secure motorcycle parking must be provided at non-residential uses of over 250 square metres.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Quantity: at least 3% of required car spaces or 4 spaces, whichever is greater.

design-code-rules.title: Accessible parking bays
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Accessible parking bays must be provided as set out in Table 16.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Streets in town and neighbourhood centres should allow for accessible parking so primary destinations are accessible to all.
design-code-rules.area-text: All place types (emphasis on Town and Neighbourhood Centres)

design-code-rules.title: Electric vehicle charging points
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Electric Vehicle charging points must be provided as set out in Table 17.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Table 17: housing 1 charge point per unit (Building Regs Approved Document S); non-residential 5% active + 5% passive spaces, at least one accessible; employment 10% active + 10% passive.

design-code-rules.title: Public cycle parking
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Public cycle parking must be provided on High Streets, local distributors and local connectors.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Other streets: private cycle parking suited to context. In town/neighbourhood centres: clusters of 3-7 stands, highly visible, 2 m clear footpath; stands 1.4 m apart (2 m for non-standard cycles); 5% of public provision for non-standard cycles (LTN 1/20 Tables 11.1-11.2).
design-code-rules.area-text: All place types (High Streets, Local Distributors, Local Connectors)

design-code-rules.title: Cycle parking for non-residential development
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Cycle parking must be provided for at least 15% of car parking spaces in non-residential development, rising to 24% in town centres.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: As close to entrance as nearest car spaces; overlooked by primary frontage, well lit, sheltered.
design-code-rules.area-text: All place types (24% in Town Centre)

design-code-rules.title: Cycle parking for new homes
design-code-rules.requirement-text: All new residential units must include a minimum of one cycle parking space.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Cycle parking must be secure, accessible and covered.

design-code-rules.title: Residential parking space sizes
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Residential parking spaces must meet the minimum sizes as set out in Table 18.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Table 18: default 2.5 x 5 m; internal garage 3 x 6 m (extra if used for cycle storage); side of house/bounded 3.2 m wide; in front of garage 2.5 x 6 m; EV space 2.8 m wide; parallel 2 x 6 m. Driveways min 3.2 m (single) / 5 m (shared); pedestrian visibility 2 x 2 m at 1.05 m high.

design-code-rules.title: Gates on driveways
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Boundary gates on on-plot parking provision must allow for inward swing of gates when all cars are parked.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Include landscaping to reduce visual impact of parking (C34).

design-code-rules.title: Position of garages and outbuildings
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Garages and outbuildings must not sit further forward than the building line of the host building.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Should not hinder natural surveillance; departures must show no negative effect on the house–street relationship; match host building materials, style and proportion; at least 6 m for a car to pull off the street and the garage door to open.

design-code-rules.title: Parking courts
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Parking courts should clearly distinguish resident and visitor spaces, include low-maintenance landscaping and benefit from natural surveillance.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Distinguish spaces via materials, design and signage; landscaping that doesn't reduce visibility, designed with SuDS (3.4); surrounding buildings provide natural surveillance (6.2).

design-code-rules.title: Distances between facing windows
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Where rear or side windows on different plots are less than 20 m apart above ground floor, or less than 14 m at ground floor, mitigation must be included to ensure privacy.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Applies between new and existing windows and multiple new plots. Options: angled windows, obscure glazing, limited opening (G14). Balconies raise the same concerns – boundary distances may need to be greater.

supporting-documents.listed-as: BRE – Site Layout Planning for Daylight and Sunlight

design-code-rules.title: Rear garden depth
design-code-rules.requirement-text: The minimum distance between the rear wall and rear boundary must be as set out in Table 19.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Minimum back-to-back distance is double this measurement. Table 19: Town Centre 7 m; Inner Neighbourhood 9 m; Outer Neighbourhood 10 m; Neighbourhood Centre 7 m; Village 10 m; Countryside 10 m.
design-code-rules.area-text: Varies by place type – Town Centre 7 m; Inner Neighbourhood 9 m; Outer Neighbourhood 10 m; Neighbourhood Centre 7 m; Village 10 m; Countryside 10 m

supporting-documents.listed-as: BRE – Site Layout Planning for Daylight and Sunlight

design-code-rules.title: Back-to-back distances on sloping sites
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Where ground levels differ, the total back-to-back distance must be increased by 2 metres for every 1 metre of height difference.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Mitigates overlooking and overshadowing from level differences.

supporting-documents.listed-as: BRE – Site Layout Planning for Daylight and Sunlight

design-code-rules.title: Overlooking and overshadowing neighbours
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Development should avoid unacceptable overlooking and overshadowing of neighbours on all sides.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Shadow depends on placement and orientation. Openings can be angled, obscure-glazed or opening-limited. Ground-floor boundary treatments can screen; seasonal planting is not acceptable for privacy.

supporting-documents.listed-as: BRE – Site Layout Planning for Daylight and Sunlight

design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Guidance only – no separate rule statement.

design-code-rules.title: Varied plot widths
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Plot widths should vary along streets; infill in conservation areas should respect historic plot patterns.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Villages and outer neighbourhoods typically show more plot-width variation than inner neighbourhoods.
design-code-rules.area-text: All place types (more variation in Village and Outer Neighbourhood than Inner Neighbourhood)

supporting-documents.listed-as: BRE – Site Layout Planning for Daylight and Sunlight

design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Guidance only.

design-code-rules.title: Side space for houses
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Detached and semi-detached houses should provide side space for access and bin movement, or for parking a car.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Min side width for parking 3.2 m (C42); min side access 0.9 m, or 1.2 m where shared by multiple dwellings (Figure 56).

supporting-documents.listed-as: BRE – Site Layout Planning for Daylight and Sunlight

design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Guidance only.

design-code-rules.title: Depth of extensions on a shared boundary
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Extensions adjoining a side boundary should not extend more than 3.5 metres past the rear elevation of the neighbouring property (single storey) or 1.5 metres (two storey).
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Sizes recommended to prevent unacceptable overshadowing/loss of light; the 45-degree rule may allow larger or smaller extensions. Further set-in from the boundary allows extra projection. Going beyond guidance must be justified. Extensions changing parking should consider Table 15 and section 7.9.

supporting-documents.listed-as: Householder version of the Design Code (PDF)

design-code-rules.title: Extensions that match the main building
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Extensions should be designed to appear as one with the main building.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Single-storey eaves max 3 m and ridge max 4 m; flat roofs use a parapet wall; multi-storey ridges below original with eaves level or lower.

supporting-documents.listed-as: Householder version of the Design Code (PDF)

design-code-rules.title: Height of front boundary treatments
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Boundary treatments for residential properties fronting public realm must not exceed 1.2 metres in height.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Tall boundaries reduce street surveillance and vehicle visibility. Higher may be justified where an established street has >1.2 m boundaries, if visibility is addressed and the plot keeps a good street relationship (Figure 59).

design-code-rules.title: Boundary treatments for homes
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Residential frontages onto the public realm should use appropriate boundary treatments.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Appropriate: green/living boundaries; brick or chalkstone walls (optionally with coping and piers); dwarf brick walls (with/without railings or hedge); low timber fence with hedgerow; metal railings (with/without hedge).
design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Guidance shown as an image.

design-code-rules.title: Landscaped boundaries in business areas
design-code-rules.requirement-text: In business and industrial areas, landscaping is preferred to distinguish site boundaries.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Where boundaries are needed consider context: thin-profile V-mesh fencing, gabion walls, living boundaries. Side/rear boundaries facing public realm should be low for passive surveillance; screen security measures with green boundaries.
design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Guidance shown as an image.

design-code-rules.title: Minimum private garden size
design-code-rules.requirement-text: There must be a minimum space standard for all private gardens, excluding gardens to the front of properties, of: 25 m² (1-3 bed) and 60 m² (4+ bed).
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Private amenity space supports play, food growing, drying washing; may be rear or side. Back-to-boundary distances (8.1) must also be met. Garages/outbuildings: C44.

design-code-rules.title: Balconies and communal space for flats
design-code-rules.requirement-text: For blocks of flats, a combination of balconies and communal amenity space should be included.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: So every home has access to outdoor space.

design-code-rules.title: Planted gardens
design-code-rules.requirement-text: All gardens should include grass, planting and other forms of vegetation to cover at least 50% of the area.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Supports wildlife, surface-water infiltration and carbon capture; green/living boundaries can increase cover.

design-code-rules.title: Bin storage for each home
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Suitable bin storage of at least 1.5 square metres must be provided per housing unit.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Within 45 m of a highway collection point; in rear garden or to side. If at front, screened by boundary treatment or integrated into building design. Based on three wheelie bins per household. Side access min 0.9 m (1.2 m shared) – see G16.

design-code-rules.title: Communal bin stores
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Communal waste bins must be stored securely in centralised areas, within 45 metres of a suitable highway collection point.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Consider screening with site landscaping; proximity to homes and noise mitigation (Figures 61-62).

design-code-rules.title: Materials for extensions
design-code-rules.requirement-text: For extensions, proposed elevational and roofing materials must match the existing colour, size, and texture of the host building.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Match type, colour and construction method; otherwise contrasting/complementary material to be discussed with officers and justified. Recreate original junction details (eaves, openings), especially for heritage assets.

supporting-documents.listed-as: Conservation Area Appraisals and Management Plans

design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Non-compliance needs justification in the application.

design-code-rules.title: Materials for new buildings
design-code-rules.requirement-text: For new buildings, materials must follow the prevailing colour, size, and texture of materials to create a cohesive palette.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Infill looks to the same street; large strategic sites develop a palette via a site design code (phases may vary). Industrial: darker tones against landscape, lighter against sky. Contemporary schemes may widen palette but reference traditional colour/texture.

supporting-documents.listed-as: Conservation Area Appraisals and Management Plans

design-code-rules.title: Main elevation facing the street
design-code-rules.requirement-text: The primary elevation must front the street. It must include the front door and windows on all levels.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Any other elevation facing the street should have windows overlooking it.

design-code-rules.title: Vertically aligned windows
design-code-rules.requirement-text: On buildings with two or more storeys, windows must align vertically through a centre point.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: No window wider or taller than the one on the floor below; windows should give habitable rooms adequate natural light.

design-code-rules.title: Window and door reveals
design-code-rules.requirement-text: All window and doors must have a minimum reveal of 70 millimetres.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Existing buildings may match existing reveals, with details set out in the application.

design-code-rules.title: Bay window projection
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Bay windows, or other window projections, must project a maximum of 1 metre from the front elevation.

design-code-rules.title: Porches and canopies over the highway
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Porches and canopies must not obstruct or overhang the public domain, or compromise visibility splays of the highway.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Porches should complement not dominate the host building; large developments should consider a mix of porch types.

design-code-rules.title: Front dormer roof form
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Dormers on front roof slopes must have gable or shed roofs.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Small flat-roofed dormers may be acceptable where the streetscene already has precedent; exceptions need justification.

design-code-rules.title: Dormer setbacks from ridge and eaves
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Dormers must be set down from the main roof ridge by a minimum of 0.2 metres and back from the eaves by a minimum of 0.2 metres.
local-plan-policies: (not listed in Appendix D) – ENV1 assumed
design-code-rules.extraction-notes: C60 appears on the 9.2 web page but is missing from the Appendix D code/policy table.

design-code-rules.title: Separate dormers on neighbouring homes
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Dormers on adjoining properties must not be, or appear to be, physically connected.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Set at least 0.2 m from the shared boundary to keep properties visually distinct.

design-code-rules.title: Dormer window alignment
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Dormer window(s) must be vertically aligned to the window(s) on the floor below; or, symmetrically aligned to the centre line of the roof.

design-code-rules.title: Dormer width
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Dormers must not exceed the width of any window on the floor below.

design-code-rules.title: Roof pitch
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Roof pitch should suit the surrounding context.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Infill can vary with existing streetscene; large strategic sites should include a range of roof heights and pitches in their site design code.
design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Guidance only.

design-code-rules.title: Roofs on two-storey extensions
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Two-storey extensions should match the original roof form and slope angle, with a lower ridge and eaves at or below the original.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: So the extension reads as subservient.
design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Guidance only.

design-code-rules.title: Chimneys on new homes
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Chimneys should be included in new residential buildings where many nearby buildings have chimneys.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Chimneys suit traditional areas and help new development fit its setting.
design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Guidance only.

design-code-rules.title: Matching windows and doors
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Alterations should match the proportions and design of existing windows and doors.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: New openings should align horizontally and vertically with existing windows where possible; exceptions justified in evidence and the compliance checklist. Window materials should match the existing building.
design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Guidance only.

design-code-rules.title: Front extensions
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Front extensions should be small, look part of the existing building and repeat its window, door and roof detailing.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Front extensions are highly visible.
design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Guidance only.

design-code-rules.title: Glazed dormer fronts
design-code-rules.requirement-text: The main face of a dormer should be mostly glazed and usually hold one centrally placed window.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Privacy impacts on neighbours must be considered (G14).
design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Guidance only.

design-code-rules.title: Dormer size, position and materials
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Dormers should be small, aligned with existing windows, and use matching materials so they don't dominate the roof.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Heritage areas need extra care; contemporary exceptions must be justified via the compliance checklist.
design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Guidance only.

design-code-rules.title: Signage on the fascia
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Principal signage must be located at the fascia.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Conservation areas: preserve/enhance traditional shopfronts, reinstating lost features; elsewhere a contemporary approach is acceptable but proportions/details still apply. A strong existing high-street precedent may justify departure – justify in evidence and compliance checklist.
design-code-rules.area-text: All place types (stricter in conservation areas)
design-code-rules.national-design-issue: Buildings - Frontages: shops, bars and eateries

design-code-rules.title: One fascia sign per bay
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Fascia signage must be limited to one per bay of unit frontage.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Conservation areas: preserve/enhance traditional shopfronts, reinstating lost features; elsewhere a contemporary approach is acceptable but proportions/details still apply. A strong existing high-street precedent may justify departure – justify in evidence and compliance checklist.
design-code-rules.area-text: All place types (stricter in conservation areas)
design-code-rules.national-design-issue: Buildings - Frontages: shops, bars and eateries

design-code-rules.title: Hanging signs
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Hanging signs must be located no higher than first floor level, projecting no more than 0.75 m forward of the unit frontage.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Assess signage harm, especially on listed buildings and in conservation areas. Prefer low-profile lighting (halo, small spotlights, compact strip); external trough lighting and internally illuminated box signs likely more harmful; individually illuminated letters may be less intrusive.
design-code-rules.area-text: All place types (stricter in conservation areas)
design-code-rules.national-design-issue: Buildings - Frontages: shops, bars and eateries

design-code-rules.title: Shopfront window panels
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Windows on frontages must have vertically proportioned panels, fixed between the stall riser and the transom bar or fascia.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Provide windows on all floors (C54).
design-code-rules.national-design-issue: Buildings - Frontages: shops, bars and eateries

design-code-rules.title: Shopfront doors
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Frontages must include a legible door access.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Use door recesses to improve legibility, following traditional arrangements.
design-code-rules.national-design-issue: Buildings - Frontages: shops, bars and eateries

design-code-rules.title: Stall risers
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Stall risers must be between 0.2-0.9 metres in height and be an integral feature of the elevation.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Conservation areas: preserve/enhance traditional shopfronts, reinstating lost features; elsewhere a contemporary approach is acceptable but proportions/details still apply. A strong existing high-street precedent may justify departure – justify in evidence and compliance checklist.
design-code-rules.national-design-issue: Buildings - Frontages: shops, bars and eateries

design-code-rules.title: Security shutters
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Security shutters must be internal and must be a grill or mesh.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Grill/mesh keeps the shop visible from the street, supporting perceptions of safety and vitality.
design-code-rules.national-design-issue: Buildings - Frontages: shops, bars and eateries

design-code-rules.title: Floors across window openings in conversions
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Floor plates must not be positioned across existing window openings.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Prevents the external appearance of openings being compromised.

supporting-documents.listed-as: Historic England – Adapting Traditional Farm Buildings

design-code-rules.title: Keeping original openings in conversions
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Original openings in the external elevations must be retained.

supporting-documents.listed-as: Historic England – Adapting Traditional Farm Buildings

design-code-rules.title: Matching materials in conversions
design-code-rules.requirement-text: New wall and roofing materials must match those in the existing building.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Conversions must not create a significant alteration or extension. Materials should match or clearly contrast, with careful detailing at junctions. Roof lights traditional in design and low profile.

supporting-documents.listed-as: Historic England – Adapting Traditional Farm Buildings

design-code-rules.title: Matching original details in conversions
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Features including lintels, key stones, brick coursing and brick types must be matched to the original.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Repair rather than replace existing features where possible.

supporting-documents.listed-as: Historic England – Adapting Traditional Farm Buildings

design-code-rules.title: Boundaries in conversions
design-code-rules.requirement-text: New boundary features must reflect existing boundary features such as hedgerows, stone and brick walls, or footpaths.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Where none exist, check historic records for former boundaries; nearby similar buildings can be a reference.

supporting-documents.listed-as: Historic England – Adapting Traditional Farm Buildings

design-code-rules.title: Visual impact of agricultural buildings
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Visual impact of buildings should be reduced, e.g. through a low-lying roof shape/roofline reflective of the landscape and topography.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Assess impact on views from within the site and from roads, footpaths, nearby properties and upland areas. Tree belts and hedgerows can soften outlines and provide shelter.
design-code-rules.area-text: All place types (agricultural sites – typically Countryside)

supporting-documents.listed-as: ILP – Bats and Artificial Lighting at Night

design-code-rules.title: Grouping agricultural buildings
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Agricultural buildings should be grouped together as to create a clearly defined plot group.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Group new buildings around a farmyard as traditional farmsteads were, where practical.

supporting-documents.listed-as: ILP – Bats and Artificial Lighting at Night

design-code-rules.title: Materials for agricultural buildings
design-code-rules.requirement-text: The materials should be appropriate for the location and use of the building.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Options: green or grey metal cladding, brick or stone matching local vernacular, Yorkshire boarding. Darker muted colours blend larger structures, especially with established landscaping.

supporting-documents.listed-as: ILP – Bats and Artificial Lighting at Night

design-code-rules.title: Lighting on rural buildings
design-code-rules.requirement-text: New lighting on rural buildings should be designed to minimise light pollution.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Keep lighting minimal and low; consider appearance from the wider landscape (esp. hillside sites); avoid harsh spotlights and large-scale floodlighting.

supporting-documents.listed-as: ILP – Bats and Artificial Lighting at Night

design-code-rules.extraction-notes: Section page links 'ENV1' to the ENV3 (heritage) URL – likely a link error.

design-code-rules.title: Views around industrial sites
design-code-rules.requirement-text: The impact of development on views from inside and outside of the site need to be considered.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Rural areas: minimal landscape impact; edge-of-town business parks may be more contemporary. Consider layout (G31), roof shape, materials, fenestration, landscaping and boundaries (G20).
design-code-rules.national-design-issue: Buildings - New industrial, storage and distribution (ISDC) buildings

supporting-documents.listed-as: ILP – Bats and Artificial Lighting at Night

design-code-rules.title: Grouping industrial buildings
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Buildings should be grouped together as to create a clearly defined plot group.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Cluster buildings to form one distinct, readable plot group.
design-code-rules.national-design-issue: Buildings - New industrial, storage and distribution (ISDC) buildings

supporting-documents.listed-as: ILP – Bats and Artificial Lighting at Night

design-code-rules.title: Materials for industrial buildings
design-code-rules.requirement-text: The materials should be appropriate for the location and use of the building.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Options: green/grey metal cladding, brick or stone matching vernacular, Yorkshire boarding; brick, concrete, steel and glass suit urban business parks. Darker muted cladding helps large structures blend.
design-code-rules.national-design-issue: Buildings - New industrial, storage and distribution (ISDC) buildings

supporting-documents.listed-as: ILP – Bats and Artificial Lighting at Night

design-code-rules.title: Lighting on industrial buildings
design-code-rules.requirement-text: New lighting should be designed to minimise light pollution.
design-code-rules.guidance-text: Assess effects on nearby homes and wildlife habitats; mount lighting as low as possible; avoid harsh spotlights and large-scale floodlighting.
design-code-rules.national-design-issue: Buildings - New industrial, storage and distribution (ISDC) buildings
